newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal rebels extend unilateral truce.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal rebels extend unilateral truce.

text.p: Separatist tribal rebels seeking autonomy for the Chittagong Hill Tracts in southeastern Bangladesh have extended a truce until end of October, a tribal statement said on Sunday.
The truce, which expires on Monday, has been unilaterally extended by the Parbatya Chhatragram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force).

The Bangladesh government, angered by last month's gruesome killing of at least 30 civilians by the guerrillas, has remained silent about the truce which, the government says, is frequently violeted by them.
The tribal insurgents abducted and massacred 30 Bengali-speaking settlers on September 10.
"The government has not requested the Shanti Bahini for the truce formally for the first time," said one security official.
He said the truce had previously been agreed upon mutually through negotiations.
The statement issued by the PCJSS said: "The truce has been extended to solve the problem politically under the purview of the sovereignity of Bangladesh."
Government officials said the unilateral declaration of the truce was a clear sign of softening of the attitude by the PCJSS which had never recognised full Bangladesh authority on the Hill Tracts.

The Shantis began an armed insurgency in the 14,200 sq-km (5,500 sq-mile) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected its demand for political autonomy in the rugged hill and forest region.
The tribals also demanded that some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers should be expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,000 civilians, rebels and soldiers have been killed in the protracted insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to flee across the border.
